title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with budget talks and infrastructure developments as various players position themselves for a shifting economic landscape. Meanwhile, the Space Force is doubling down on its funding and capabilities, while private firms are racing to deliver advanced satellite solutions.

themes.title: Budget Battles Heat Up
themes.body: Trump's proposed budget increase for the Space Force is stirring discussions about the future of military space funding. The FY27 markup adds $1.4 billion to enhance space resilience, indicating a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space.

themes.title: Infrastructure Investment Trends
themes.body: Companies like Bluestaq and Swissto12 are stepping up to build the necessary infrastructure for a burgeoning space economy. Their efforts reflect a broader trend of private sector involvement in what was once solely a government domain.

themes.title: Defense Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window is showing signs of life, with companies like Palantir securing significant extensions on contracts. This could signal a shift in investor sentiment towards the defense sector as it adapts to new technological demands.

themes.title: Space Development Agency Moves Forward
themes.body: The Space Development Agency is ramping up its efforts with new awards for missile defense tracking satellites. This initiative underscores the urgency of enhancing national security through advanced space capabilities.
